terms.comment: From sufflāmen, the drag on a wheel (Juv. 8.148 rotam adstringit sufflāmine).

terms.gloss: a brake; classically a drag on a wheel
evidence: Juv. 8.148: rotam astringit multō sufflāmine (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Sufflāmen is the classical drag-chain or brake on a wheel (Juv., Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quotiēns avus ad sēmaphorum rubrum rotās sufflāminābat
phrases.english: every time Grandpa braked at a red light

sources: Lexicon Latinum Hodiernum: bicycle parts · Morgan–Owens: Silva

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 215, 325.
